subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Traction Control Systems
description: Learn Traction Control Systems in one minute.

hook.text: Even skilled drivers can spin the wheels on a wet or icy road without realizing it.

buildup.text: Wheelspin wastes engine power and can send a car sideways in a fraction of a second.

discovery.text: Traction control detects when a wheel spins too fast and cuts engine power instantly.

twist.text: Early systems were so aggressive they made cars sluggish—some drivers turned them off.

climax.text: Modern traction control adjusts dozens of times per second, keeping grip invisibly.

punchline.text: The system you never notice saves you the most.

quiz.question: What does traction control do when it detects wheelspin?
options: Cuts engine power or brakes the wheel

details.summary: Traction control systems detect spinning wheels during acceleration and reduce engine power or apply brakes to those wheels, helping drivers maintain grip on slippery or uneven road surfaces.
details.whyItMatters: Loss of traction during acceleration causes skids and loss of vehicle control. Traction control provides a critical safety net in rain, snow, and ice by keeping driven wheels from spinning freely.
takeaways: Sensors detect when a wheel spins faster than the others
The system cuts engine power or brakes the spinning wheel
Traction control works alongside ABS using the same sensors

faq.question: Is traction control the same as all-wheel drive?
faq.answer: No. All-wheel drive sends power to all four wheels, while traction control manages wheel spin on whichever wheels receive power. They complement each other but are separate systems.

faq.question: Should traction control ever be turned off?
faq.answer: In deep snow, sand, or mud, some wheel spin is needed to gain momentum. Turning off traction control in these specific situations can help the car get unstuck. On normal roads it should stay on.
